idiom_name: TypeScript class + #private fields, one concept per module
implementation_notes: The class keeps the concept's data and behaviour in one declaration and #private fields make the representation unreachable at runtime (TypeScript's private is erased, so structural typing and emitted JavaScript can still reach those members). Because types disappear at runtime, the class body is the only place where a concept's state and methods are actually co-located; prefer it when the concept has identity, mutation and invariants worth protecting from the rest of the codebase.
pitfalls: private (without #) is compile-time only and ignored by structural typing: another object with the same shape is assignable, so invariants need #private fields or nominal branding.
#private fields are invisible to spread and JSON serialization, so DTO mapping must be written explicitly.

variants.name: Data type + module-scoped functions
variants.idiom_name: one module per concept: data type + smart constructor + pure operations
variants.implementation_notes: The module is the contour: a type or interface declares the concept, a smart constructor validates it, and every operation is a function in the same file that returns a new value instead of mutating (the official handbook notes that free functions working over data are the natural style in JS/TS, with classes as one valid option). Choose it when the concept is a value or a closed union and behaviour is computation - the classic OO form is justified when identity and controlled mutation are the point.
pitfalls: Nothing stops callers from constructing the type literal directly, so the smart constructor only works if the type is branded or the raw type is not exported.
Discriminated unions grow a switch at every call site; without exhaustive helpers, a new variant is handled in some functions and silently skipped in others.
